info.desc: Weezer (commonly known as the Blue Album) is the eponymous debut studio album by American rock band Weezer, released on May 10, 1994 by DGC Records. The album came two years after the band's founding, after they initially struggled as an alternative to grunge music, which was prevalent in Los Angeles during the early 1990s. It was almost entirely arranged and composed by frontman Rivers Cuomo, who also anticipated to lead the band in self-producing the album. However, at the behest of DGC, the band was required to include a producer, and collectively opted for Cars frontman Ric Ocasek. Most .

podcast.body: Referred to as "the blue one," this debut album features the song "My Name Is Jonas" and is an early showcase of Weezer's embrace of their geekiness, which they continued to celebrate in their subsequent work. "Weezer from their debut album, which is the blue one, and my name is Jonas."

podcast.title: Multi-Million Selling Debut
podcast.body: Released in 1994, Weezer's debut album, commonly known as the "Blue Album," went on to sell over 15 million copies. Its success was significantly bolstered by songs like "Buddy Holly," which, despite initial reluctance from Rivers Cuomo, was included after persuasion from producer Ric Ocasek and the rest of the band. "And that debut blue album would later go on to sell somewhere north of 15 million copies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
